# DNS-Shaped Keys: Expanse vs. BTreeMap and QP-Trie

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_readme.py from results/baseline_*.json; do not edit by hand. -->

`ExpanseOrderedBytesMap` against `std::collections::BTreeMap` and [`qp-trie`](https://github.com/sdleffler/qp-trie-rs) `=0.8.2` on domain names stored as reversed-label keys: exact lookup, the predecessor lookup behind a denial-of-existence answer, closest encloser, live heap, and predecessor lookups from concurrent readers. The suite measures the index alone, on synthetic names. Design, arms, pre-registration and claims ceiling: [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md); tracking issue [#1800](https://github.com/orieg/expanse/issues/1800).

## Provenance

No reference-host run is committed yet; every table below is empty and every verdict is pending the two dispatches METHODOLOGY.md §4 requires ([#1800](https://github.com/orieg/expanse/issues/1800)).

## Reproduce

```bash
docs/benchmarks/dns_names/run.sh          # full run, on the Linux reference host
docs/benchmarks/dns_names/run.sh --quick  # smoke run into results/quick/ (gitignored)
python3 docs/benchmarks/dns_names/scripts/generate_readme.py
```

On a pull request, `/benchmark dns_names` runs the same runner on the bare-metal host. The harnesses are `crates/expanse/benches/dns_*.rs`; each carries its `# Workload shape` table.
